newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Injured Bangladeshi in Bahrain arson attack dies.
newsitem.headline: Injured Bangladeshi in Bahrain arson attack dies.

text.p: A Bangladeshi man died in hospital on Tuesday, raising the death toll in an arson attack this week in Bahrain to two, a government official said.
"The man died in hospital this morning," the official told Reuters.
A Bangladeshi worker died when a group of people set a store ablaze on Saturday in Sitra, linked with the capital Manama by a three km (1.8 mile) causeway.
The fire was one of several recent arson attacks in Bahrain, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre and headquarters of the U.S. Fifth Fleet which patrols the oil-rich Gulf region.
On Tuesday an official said a restaurant was destroyed in an apparent arson attack the previous day. No one was injured.
"The fire took place on Monday and completely gutted the restaurant. There were no casualties," he told Reuters. "Initial indications showed the fire was a sabotage act."
A power generator blew up at a luxury hotel on Saturday, but there were no reports of damage or casualties.
On Friday, a restaurant was set ablaze in a Manama district and three other fires broke out in Muharraq, linked with Manama by another three km (1.8 miles) causeway.
Four Indians died from smoke inhalation and a fifth was critically injured after fire gutted a shop in Manama in June.
The attacks in early June were described by a government official as "continued acts of terrorism."

Members of the islands's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to press the Sunni-led government to introduce economic and political reforms.
